caption:
Anxiety. Low mood. A sleep problem. Then, years later, ADHD.

Studies suggest many adults are diagnosed with anxiety, depression or a sleep problem before ADHD is recognised. Emotional ups and downs, poor sleep and restlessness are part of adult ADHD for many people, and they overlap with other conditions. A careful assessment follows the timeline back to childhood, to understand what came first.

Part of our series, ADHD: the full picture.

Research:
Long, N., & Coats, H. (2022). The need for earlier recognition of ADHD in primary care. https://doi.org/10.1093/fampra/cmac038
Okada, T., et al. (2024). Psychiatric comorbidities of ADHD in Japan: A nationwide population-based study. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyt.2024.1359872
